This is happening against a brutal backdrop: the 10Y yield has surged to 4.80% (↑3.9%), oil has spiked to $90.93 (↑20.9% on Iran war re-escalation), equities are bleeding (S&P ↓0.8%, Russell 2000 ↓2.4%, Nasdaq ↓1.4%), and the Gold/BTC ratio has collapsed to 0.0573 with a -17.6 percentage point divergence showing BTC massively outrunning gold as the preferred macro hedge.
Headlines about mortgage rates surging "double digits as Iran war reescalates," bond supply problems pushing yields higher, and warnings about economic downturns are all fueling the flight into BTC.

Retail discourse is framing BTC not as speculation but as survival — "bonds are uninvestable," "5% yields mean the government can't afford its debt," "Bitcoin fixes this." Reddit and fintwit are circulating the Peter Schiff Treasury warning as confirmation of the debasement thesis.

The mechanical similarity is that retail is front-running what they believe will be forced institutional capitulation: if yields keep surging and bonds keep selling off, institutions will eventually need non-correlated assets, and BTC is the one with the most reflexive upside.
However, many quant desks see BTC's surge as a liquidity mirage: with yields at 4.80% and rising, risk-free rates are creating enormous opportunity cost for holding a zero-yield asset.

When the narrative breaks: The trade dies if any of three things happen: (1) a ceasefire or de-escalation in the Iran conflict collapses oil back below $80, removing the geopolitical panic bid; (2) the Fed or Treasury announces credible yield-curve-control measures or emergency bond buying that stabilizes the long end and makes Treasuries attractive again — killing the "bonds are uninvestable" thesis; or (3) the 10Y yield breaches 5.00% so aggressively that it triggers a genuine liquidity crisis and margin calls that force liquidation of all risk assets including BTC, as happened in crypto's 2022 crash.
